Reply "O-26 option 2", "option 2 and 3", or something else. Approved". Rule text: R-LI and R-LH keep their rule and gain one door. An EXISTING hand-authored oracle file (status modified, extension `ts`, `tsx`, `mjs`, `js` or `json`) may change in a commit, or in a push or CI range, that also changes CODE only when ALL of these hold. (1) The prereg of the round's loop record (found by the gate's lookup (R-KV as amended by R-MA)) lists in `expected_value_changes[]` every changed line of that file; when a push or CI range adds several records, the lists of all of their preregs, each found by the same lookup for its own record, together cover the changed lines; a record of the range whose prereg the lookup does not find never passes. One entry `{path, case, old, new, ruling, ruling_ref}` per changed line: a replacement is one entry with both `old` and `new`; a pure addition has `old` null; a pure deletion has `new` null; not both null. (2) Each `ruling` is a register row `M-nnn` or `P-nnn` that the register shows as RATIFIED or RULED ("RULED" here means RATIFIED or RULED, as `parseRulings` reads them) at the parent of the prereg's first commit AND still at the round's revision, whose row, with its dated-note rows (the directly following lines that start `\| \|`, up to the next id row), cites `ruling_ref` in the register's own form `<log stem>#<ref>`, where `docs/reports/decisions/<stem>.json` holds that decision. At commit and push (NOT in CI) the row with that citation must also already be in a remote-tracking ref of `origin` (`refs/remotes/origin/*`): the register read at the merge base of that ref and the prereg's parent shows the same id RATIFIED or RULED with the citation. A ruling that exists only in the branch being gated never counts at commit and push. In CI the decision log is read at the prereg's parent only. (3) Path by path, the changed lines of the diff (blank lines ignored, each line trimmed, comments counted) equal the listed lines exactly as multisets, none more and none fewer; a modified file whose diff has no changed line, or carries a mode, rename, copy, binary or submodule header, does not pass. (4) The prereg was committed once, alone, strictly before every change to each path it lists, and its content is the same at the tip as at its first commit (a deleted prereg is a changed prereg). (5) Each entry's `case` contains a case token, a run matching `[A-Za-z]{1,3}[0-9]{3,}` or the basename of its path without extension, that occurs verbatim in the cited ruling's row (with its dated-note rows) or in the cited decision's `question`, `recommendation` or `operator_quote`; the row and the decision are read at the pushed commit (the merge base), and in CI at the prereg's parent. `case` is otherwise a label for the operator's reading, not authority. A deleted, renamed, copied or type-changed oracle file (in ANY commit of the range), a prereg file, an oracle file added in the same range and edited again in it (net status A), or any check that cannot be read never passes: the gate says `oracle_moved_with_code` plus the reason, and exits red or "cannot run". Adding a new oracle file beside code stays allowed. What the door does and does not do: it stops an agent that only commits locally, and an edit whose citation, ruling or case token does not exist. It does not stop an agent with a shell from faking a remote-tracking ref of `origin` (`git update-ref`), it does not evaluate the pushed-ref condition in CI, it ties an entry to its ruling by one shared token only, and it does not prove that the edit is what the ruling meant. The authority is the operator's approval of the push that carried the ruling and the operator's reading of the lines at the push prompt. Today the pre-push summary prints one line per file (`path +added -deleted`) and its EXPECTED ANSWERS MOVED flag does not cover `src/tests/bylaw-*.test.ts`, so the summary does not show the changed lines. The loop output that the hook prints before the push prompt does: the gate's pass note prints one line per listed entry, `oracle_door_entry:<path>: <old> -> <new>  [<ruling> #<ref>]`, capped at 12 lines and then a "more" line, and before the first door-using push the orchestrator shows the operator the entries (for item a, the 11) in chat. A named follow-up in `scripts/analysis/mcbylaws/**` (MB-67-owned, outside this item) adds the entries to the pre-push summary itself. `expected_value_changes[]` here means oracle lines; the "zero moves" of R-LZ means zero ROW moves (`expected_moves`, `expected_moves_4d`) and is not affected by this list. Five words: standardized (one door, one list shape, one equality); observable (the lock is named: loop-gate oracle-door red fixtures (MB-79 (f)); every pass prints the ruling, its ref and the number of listed changes); scalable (any file, rule and increment; no id in code); accurate (O-26: A0399 side yard 1.2 -> 0.6, ruled CHAT-210.MB17-Q1R beside code, the values named by the M-180 dated note of O-30); understandable (list the changed lines, cite a ruling already on the origin remote, commit it first). No scope beyond the cards (M-328).
